title: A Spire for the Hollow
premise: Freya Nakamura keeps the Hollow Gate sealed beneath the city of Vess and sells harmless charms to survive in a kingdom that has outlawed magic. When the usurper King Aldous launches a kingdom-wide hunt for the gifted, Freya is betrayed by a customer and forced to flee with a ragged band of outcasts who become the family he never had. As the usurper's armies march toward the free cities, Freya discovers the Gate is the only thing keeping an ancient war from reigniting — and that opening it could save his found family but doom the world. In the end, Freya chooses truth over loyalty to his companions, seals the Gate at the cost of his own gift, and the free cities hold, though the family he found must learn to love a keeper who can no longer do magic.
about_author: Jonah Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forbidden grimoires before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about people who keep secrets too heavy to carry alone.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Morning
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya sells a luck charm to a nervous young woman in the market, hiding the hum of magic beneath his skin, then descends at night to check the Hollow Gate's seals. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath ordinary life — the reader feels how fragile his double existence is.

chapters.title: Proclamations on Every Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The crown posts edicts: all gifted persons must register or be hunted. Freya's neighbor and only friend, the baker Tomas, burns a warning into his doorstep. Emotional beat: the noose tightening; Freya realizes his three quiet years are over.

chapters.title: The Customer Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The young charm buyer returns, reveals she is a crown informant, and names him before the wardens. Freya flees through Vess's rooftops as Tomas covers his escape and is taken. Emotional beat: betrayal and guilt — survival begins by costing him someone.

chapters.title: Outcasts on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. On the road east, Freya falls in with three fugitives: Brannic, a disgraced warden; Isolde, a hedge-witch with a child's gift of mending; and Pip, a street thief who can whisper to locks. Emotional beat: wary, prickly first bonds forming among strangers.

chapters.title: What the Gate Keeps
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. She notices Freya's seal-scars and deduces he is a Gatekeeper. Freya confesses the Hollow Gate's purpose: it holds back the Old Powers the first kings bound. Emotional beat: the secret shared — trust given before it is earned, and the stakes made cosmic.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Hounds
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Warden-captain Serah Vane, Brannic's former protégée, tracks the group with scent-hounds and cold certainty. An ambush at a river ford is survived only by Pip's lock-whispering. Emotional beat: the hunter becomes personal; Brannic's shame at what the wardens have become.

chapters.title: A Family Made of Necessity
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Sheltering in a ruined waystation, the four share stories over a fire — losses, betrayals, reasons they ran. Pip, who has never had a home, quietly decides these people are his. Emotional beat: found family solidifying into something worth dying for.

chapters.title: The Free Cities' Door
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The group reaches Mereth, first of the free cities, and petitions its council for sanctuary. The council is divided: harbor the gifted and invite invasion, or trade them for peace. Emotional beat: hope curdling into politics; the free world is not what Freya imagined.

chapters.title: Serah Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. In Vess, Serah interrogates Tomas and learns Freya is no ordinary charm-seller but the last Gatekeeper. She requests leave to hunt him personally, hiding from Aldous why the Gate matters. Emotional beat: the antagonist gains depth and a hidden agenda.

chapters.title: The Council's Bargain
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The council offers sanctuary in exchange for Freya opening the Hollow Gate to weaponize what lies beyond it against Aldous. Freya refuses; the council threatens expulsion. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth sharpened — his friends' safety is now the price of his silence.

chapters.title: Night of Broken Seals
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Aldous's forces strike Mereth's outer wall early; in the chaos, Freya feels the Hollow Gate's seals weakening across the distance — someone is unbinding them. Emotional beat: dread; the choice may already be out of his hands.

chapters.title: The Road Back to Vess
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. The group votes to return to Vess to reseal the Gate, knowing it means walking into the hunt's heart. Pip steals maps; Isolde brews concealment draughts. Emotional beat: resolve — the family chooses each other and the world at once.

chapters.title: Tomas in the Warden Cells
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Infiltrating Vess, Freya finds Tomas alive but broken by interrogation, and learns Serah let him live as bait. Freya must leave him to keep the mission. Emotional beat: the cruelest cost yet; guilt as a companion he cannot put down.

chapters.title: Beneath the Hollow
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya descends to the Gate and finds Serah already there — not unbinding it, but trying to reseal it herself, taught by her grandmother, a keeper of the old line. Emotional beat: enemy and mirror; Serah reveals Aldous wants the Gate opened deliberately.

chapters.title: The Usurper's True Design
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah explains Aldous believes the Old Powers will crown him as their war-king if he opens the Gate with keeper's blood. She defects, handing Freya her grandmother's sealing rites. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance; the truth finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Captured by Aldous's vanguard, Pip is offered his friends' lives in exchange for the Gate's location — and, terrified, gives it. Emotional beat: loyalty fractured by fear; Pip's shame sets up the climax's stakes.

chapters.title: The Army at the Gate
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Aldous's army descends into the Hollow with Pip's information. Isolde's mending gift shields the retreat; Brannic holds the stair against his former brothers-in-arms. Emotional beat: desperate, bloody defense — the family paying the price of survival in full.

chapters.title: Keeper's Blood
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Aldous drags Freya to the Gate and cuts his palm for the opening rite. The Old Powers press through the widening seam — an ancient war's first breath. Emotional beat: the lowest point; Freya's secret has become the world's wound.

chapters.title: The Choice of Truth
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya tells his friends the full truth: resealing requires burning out a keeper's gift forever — he will never work magic again. They refuse to let him; Pip confesses his betrayal and begs to take his place. Emotional beat: love confronting sacrifice; truth over protection.

chapters.title: Sealing the Hollow
chapters.summary: Freya, Serah, and Isolde's amplified rites clash with Aldous at the Gate's mouth. Pip's whisper unbinds Aldous's ward-stone; Brannic cuts the usurper down as the Powers recoil. Freya pours his gift into the seals. Emotional beat: climax — victory purchased with everything Freya was.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The Gate is shut; the magic is gone from Freya, and the hunt collapses with Aldous dead. The free cities debate what to do with the gifted; Serah pledges to reform the wardens. Emotional beat: exhausted grief and fragile hope; the war that never was, mourned anyway.

chapters.title: A House Without Charms
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A year later, Freya runs a bakery with Tomas in Mereth, magicless and content; Pip, Isolde, Brannic, and Serah gather for midwinter supper. Freya visits the sealed Gate one last time and feels nothing — and is glad. Emotional beat: resolution — family chosen, truth survived, peace earned.
